historical_cases.question: What is the investment thesis for ASML Holding NV, what supports it, and what could invalidate it? Distinguish reported facts from inference and cite material claims.
historical_cases.direct_answer:
Financial thesis foundation (partial)

Conditional financial case: sustaining the favorable reported trends in revenue from contracts with customers excluding assessed taxes [E1], operating income [E2], net income attributable to parent [E3], operating cash flow [E4] would support the financial foundation of the investment case.

Reported evidence
1. ASML revenue from contracts with customers excluding assessed taxes increased 15.6% to 32.7B EUR for the period 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31, from 28.3B EUR in the comparable prior-year period 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-31. [E1]

2. ASML operating income increased 25.3% to 11.3B EUR for the period 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31, from 9B EUR in the comparable prior-year period 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-31. [E2]

3. ASML net income attributable to parent increased 26.9% to 9.6B EUR for the period 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31, from 7.6B EUR in the comparable prior-year period 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-31. [E3]

4. ASML operating cash flow increased 13.4% to 12.7B EUR for the period 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31, from 11.2B EUR in the comparable prior-year period 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-31. [E4]

Interpretation and conditional tests
Reported revenue from contracts with customers excluding assessed taxes is higher than the comparable prior-year amount. [E1] A future comparable revenue from contracts with customers excluding assessed taxes below the cited current amount would weaken this financial assumption; this is a monitoring condition, not a forecast.

Reported operating income is higher than the comparable prior-year amount. [E2] A future comparable operating income below the cited current amount would weaken this financial assumption; this is a monitoring condition, not a forecast.

Reported net income attributable to parent is higher than the comparable prior-year amount. [E3] A future comparable net income attributable to parent below the cited current amount would weaken this financial assumption; this is a monitoring condition, not a forecast.

Reported operating cash flow is higher than the comparable prior-year amount. [E4] A future comparable operating cash flow below the cited current amount would weaken this financial assumption; this is a monitoring condition, not a forecast.

Operating-margin evidence for competitive assessment
Calculated operating margin widened by 2.67 percentage points: 34.60% for 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31, versus 31.92% for 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-31. Formula: operating income / revenue × 100, using the cited consolidated reported amounts in each period; displayed margins are rounded to two decimals. This is within-issuer profitability evidence, not a peer comparison or proof of pricing power, market share or durable competitive advantage. The drivers of the margin change remain unverified. [E1] [E2] A future comparable margin below the cited current margin would weaken the profitability assumption. Review pricing, costs and product mix, and comparable peer evidence, before drawing a competitive-strength conclusion; this is not a forecast.

Official business, competition and sampled risk context
ASML described its business in its 20-F filed 2026-02-25: “To help our customers understand and correct potential variations or errors, we provide support and solutions at every stage of the chipmaking process – from early design and development to high- volume production.” This is an issuer description; competitive advantage and future performance remain unverified. [E5]

ASML described competition in its 20-F filed 2026-02-25: “We compete primarily with Canon and Nikon in respect of DUV systems.” This is issuer-reported competitive context; relative strength, market share and durable advantage remain unverified. [E6]

ASML described competition in its 20-F filed 2026-02-25: “We also face competition from new competitors with substantial financial resources, as well as from those driven by the ambition of self-sufficiency in the geopolitical context.” This is issuer-reported competitive context; relative strength, market share and durable advantage remain unverified. [E7]

ASML disclosed in its 20-F filed 2026-02-25: “Suppliers may be unable or unwilling to commit the necessary resources for continued (co-)development, which has led and can continue to lead to ASML funding these R&D efforts or limiting our own investment capacity.” This is an issuer disclosure, not an independent assessment of whether the described effects occurred or will occur, or of their financial impact. [E8]

ASML disclosed in its 20-F filed 2026-02-25: “Patent rights will expire, which may result in key technology becoming widely available, which may harm our competitive position.” This is an issuer disclosure, not an independent assessment of whether the described effects occurred or will occur, or of their financial impact. [E9]
These short excerpts are partial context, not a complete business model or a ranking of the most material risks. Disclosed possibilities do not establish occurrence, probability or a quantified effect on the financial case.

The operating-margin comparison uses matched revenue and operating-income periods and filing versions. No cash-conversion ratio or causal relationship has been established.

This financial foundation does not establish a complete investment thesis or a buy/sell recommendation. Unverified requested parts: competitive position; valuation and expected returns; risk materiality, likelihood and effect on the investment case.
